ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 40:60 ratio of high-intensity (white) to low-intensity (dark/black) pixels, with high-intensity pixels concentrated on the lateral-distal wings and low-intensity pixels concentrated in the central peduncle region.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous white fields on the outer 40% of both lobes. The left lobe contains a distinctive dark circular pixel cluster (annulus) within its white field. The right lobe exhibits a more striated and fragmented white-to-black transition toward the trailing edge.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Broad U-shaped notch with an estimated pixel angle of 115 degrees and a vertical depth of approximately 6% of the total visible fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Irregular serrations along the entire trailing edge boundary; moderate frequency with high-amplitude jagged peaks visible at the extreme distal tips where the contour becomes highly fragmented.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: The trailing edge follows a symmetrical upward convexity from the median notch, terminating in sharp upward-pointing distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Dense, high-contrast white clusters of raised relief pixels at the distal tips of both lobes, consistent with barnacle colonization patterns.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: A single prominent, vertical high-intensity linear mark (rake mark or scratch) located on the lower-left ventral surface, approximately one-third of the distance from the notch to the left tip.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A circular dark mark located in the upper-left lobe's white field; a distinct vertical white linear scar on the lower-left ventral surface; notable tissue fragmentation/jaggedness at the distal-most points.
other_distinctive_markers: The eye-like dark focal spot located within the high-intensity white patch on the left lobe is a highly unique visual marker.
